claims.statement: Battery passports become mandatory for relevant categories on 18 February 2027, creating a paid compliance event for producers and importers.

The EU registry stores identifiers and metadata while operators remain responsible for decentralized product data and may use service providers, leaving a hosting and evidence-operation layer to supply.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Battery producer/importer compliance, product or IT lead
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Polish-language onboarding, supplier evidence collection and managed exception handling; generic DPP platforms can bundle all of it
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: unknown today; proposed future ownership by the prospective business under direct producer contracts
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Battery compliance consultants, testing labs and targeted outbound

fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Assumption: implementation fee upfront and annual hosting prepaid
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 65-80% after cloud, support and specialist review
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Data mapping, onboarding and exception review; 5,000-20,000 PLN per account assumed
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Security audits, legal review, insurance and backup obligations; certification requirements unknown
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Implementation fee plus annual per-SKU or per-passport subscription
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Cloud storage, QR/data carriers, API operations and compliance specialist time

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: ERP, PLM and established DPP vendors add battery modules and price aggressively
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Mandatory passport registration before covered batteries are placed on the EU market
commercial_mechanics.payer: Battery producer, importer or responsible economic operator
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Covered battery launch, import or 2027 compliance readiness
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual hosting renewal, new models and continuing passport updates

contrary_evidence: Large manufacturers may self-host or extend existing PLM systems.
Certification and backup-service rules may favor established providers.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: No current rights; proposed workflow-integration agreement with each responsible operator
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Serve another battery niche or sell readiness/data-mapping projects without hosting
critical_control_point.current_owner: Responsible operators own product evidence; EU authorities control the registry
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: unknown today; proposed future ownership by the prospective business under direct producer contracts
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No present battery-producer data access or customer contract
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business only after customer authorization and registry-compatible implementation
critical_control_point.renewal: unknown; proposed automatic annual renewal subject to termination terms
critical_control_point.subject: Hosted battery-passport evidence and registry workflow

economics.acquisition_route: Sell paid readiness mappings to 3 Polish battery importers, then convert one repeatable schema into hosted service
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 250 accounts at 35,000 PLN ARR and 72% gross margin could support 2m+ PLN EBITDA; at 4-6x, founder value can pass 5m PLN in years 6-9. Market concentration and price are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 20 hours weekly for MVP; specialist onboarding must be hired after 10-15 accounts
economics.gross_margin_basis: Subscription and implementation revenue less cloud, support and specialist validation
economics.payback: Assumption: 5-8 implementation customers recover setup within 18 months
economics.pricing: Assumption: 15,000-50,000 PLN implementation plus 12,000-60,000 PLN annual subscription
economics.retention_or_repeat: Regulatory record continuity, new SKUs and supplier updates

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable battery schemas and supplier-evidence resolution history
fingerprint.customer: Polish and CEE battery producers and importers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Compliance-lab and consultant referrals plus direct sales
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Managed battery-passport hosting and evidence operations subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Responsible operator pays before placing a covered battery on the market
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A hard 2027 passport deadline meets fragmented supplier data

founder_fit: Data engineering and AI-assisted document extraction are strong matches.
Low-capital MVP is possible alongside employment.

structure.commercial_archetype: Vertical compliance SaaS with managed onboarding
structure.critical_dependency: Producer adoption and authoritative supplier data

thesis: Future state: every covered battery entering the EU carries a maintained passport. The missing operational mechanism for smaller producers is a secure evidence-to-registry workflow that continuously resolves supplier data gaps.
title: Battery-Passport Host for CEE Producers
